answer.rationale: memory_c2 confirms the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing last year; memory_c4 confirms renegotiation recovers real margin via benchmarking. The primary contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, finance mandates an 18% cut, and the low-cost vendor's quote alone meets that mandate. Because the assembly line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer (per memory_c3 logic, adding a second source removed single-point failure and allocation held through shortage), a guarded scale-up to the low-cost vendor as primary is the lowest-TCO path that doesn't raise delivery risk.
